sources.outlet: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (news release, investigation update)
sources.quote: and multiple explosions and fires, and ultimately the release of 31,525 pounds of EtO, a cancer-causing substance.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest source found with a pound figure: the July 14, 2023 Glycol II explosion released 31,525 lb EtO (lead: 32,106 lb 'leaks', 34,369 lb total for 2023). Confirms the spike is one upset event.

sources.outlet: The Advocate (Baton Rouge), David J. Mitchell
sources.quote: released nearly a decade’s worth of typical emissions of the flammable and potent carcinogen ethylene oxide
sources.searcher_note: Same sentence continues '– more than 31,000 pounds -- along with 16 other chemicals in 12 hours.' Frames the 2023 release as ~10 years of normal emissions (lead: 8.7x its 2015-22 high).

sources.quote: The only plant that released more ethylene oxide than Indorama’s Port Neches facility in 2023 was Dow Chemical’s ethane cracker in Plaquemine, Louisiana.
sources.searcher_note: Ranks Dow Plaquemine #1 US ethylene oxide emitter in 2023 (EPA TRI review). No pound figure or national share for Dow.

sources.outlet: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (news release, final report)
sources.quote: resulting in the release of more than 31,000 pounds of toxic EtO, which is produced at the facility.
sources.searcher_note: Final CSB report: cause was work lights left in a reflux drum; shelter-in-place for hundreds of residents.

sources.quote: by Dow Chemical in the town of Plaquemine, in Iberville Parish, the nation’s top ethylene oxide emitter
sources.searcher_note: Op-ed calls Dow Plaquemine the nation's top EtO emitter; no year or pounds given in the quoted line.

sources.quote: On Nov. 6, 2022, the facility accidentally released 10,302 pounds of ethylene, 765 pounds of ethylene oxide and 11,774 pounds of methane into the atmosphere when the Glycol 2 unit lost power after a circuit breaker tripped.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest coverage found, two weeks after the explosion: LDEQ records of prior Glycol 2 EtO releases (765 lb 2022, ~29 lb 2019, 26 lb 2020); no pound figure yet for the July 2023 event. Live page 403s to bots; text confirmed in the Internet Archive copy.

notes: The 2023 spike is the July 14, 2023 Glycol II explosion, widely covered and quantified by CSB (31,525 lb, June 2024) and press (The Advocate 2026: 'more than 31,000 pounds', 'nearly a decade's worth'). No source found stating the lead's 34,369 lb annual total, the 21% share of the 2023 national total (160,219 lb), or the 2024 drop to 2,433 lb. Hunterbrook (2026-06-26) and a Lens op-ed call Dow Plaquemine the top US EtO emitter. Also seen, not recorded: Louisiana Illuminator 2023-08-23 on LDEQ's $120,000 settlement signed July 6, 2023 for pre-explosion violations; Dow SEC 10-Q/10-K note EPA RMP notice letter (Jan 3, 2025) alleging 21 violations tied to the incident. Coverage dated after 2026-06-30: none found.
